raj.kapoor: Heads-up — audit-ingest showed sustained backpressure this morning (~4x normal). high fanout from 3 tenants and some large user_action payloads. anyone digging?

 eva.li: saw the spike at 09:12 UTC. indexer queue climbed, ES bulk rejects increased. not sure if producers suddenly changed schema or just a traffic pattern.

 sarah-ng: could be hot shards. we currently shard by timestamp -> ES routing. if a tenant emits bursts, one shard gets crushed. can we shard by tenant prefix + small hash?

 peter-w: we already include tenant_id in the outgoing envelope but it was optional. proposal: make tenant_id required and add an ingest-computed field `event_shard` so routing is deterministic. also add `sensitive: bool` flag for opt-in encrypted payloads. sample event proto: 

 ```json
 {
   "tenant_id": "t-123",
   "event_type": "user_action",
   "payload": { "user_id": "u-9", "action": "login" },
   "event_shard": 3,
   "sensitive": false
 }
 ```

 kim-choi: question on KMS: some audit events include PII. do we expect to call KMS per event to envelope-encrypt payloads? per-event KMS calls will kill latency and cost.

 eva.li: agreed — KMS per event is not acceptable. options we discussed: 1) batch-level envelope encryption (one KMS decrypt per batch), 2) require producers to redact PII, 3) use a local HSM/KEK to do fast bulk encrypt then rotate keys via KMS periodically.

 raj.kapoor: I think we should not block schema rollout on perfect KMS flow. plan: 1) make tenant_id required + add event_shard, 2) enable bulk ingest/batching and prefix caching to reduce ES pressure, 3) add `sensitive` opt-in that routes events to a different pipeline until we have an efficient KMS pattern.

 peter-w: for customer-facing validation behavior: validator should return 4xx for schema errors, 202 Accepted for valid but queued, and include a `validation_reason` string in the response for debugging. also add a non-breaking mode where unknown fields are dropped and logged (opt-in).

 ops-bot: incident-bot created #inc-202-17654321: audit-ingest backpressure (alerting to eng-sre + eng-security).

 sarah-ng: cost note — with current steady-state volume the ES storage + indexing is ~ $12k/mo in dev account. switching to bulk indexing and increasing batch size reduces write ops ~6x in our sim. need to recalc with new shard strategy.

 kim-choi: vuln triage note — if payloads marked `sensitive` are mistakenly logged unencrypted anywhere, escalate to P1 and run incident playbook + customer notification. document the threat model in the PR.

 eva.li: rollout plan: canary 5% tenants with new schema and shard routing, monitor p95/p99 latency, ES queue depth, and error rate. if queue depth falls and tails improve -> ramp. fallback: route to cold storage + async reindexer to avoid data loss.

 raj.kapoor: action items — peter-w to open PR for schema + validator, eva.li to prototype batch-envelope encryption and doc perf tradeoffs, sarah-ng to run updated cost sims with shard + batch params, kim-choi to draft KMS threat model & incident steps. i'll coordinate canary gating.

 peter-w: will send PR today, includes migration guide + compatibility tests.

 sarah-ng: i'll run sims and post numbers (cost/latency) in this thread by EOD.

 kim-choi: adding the vulnerability checklist to the PR description.

 eva.li: +1 on canary first. also, add metrics for `events:encrypted` and `events:sensitive_dropped`.

 raj.kapoor: thanks all. ping me if you hit blockers. :thumbsup:
